Q: "Is it possible that the EM drive gets its thrust by magnifying and accelerating radio or sound waves?" A: No.

First of all, radio waves are not at all involved in "the EM drive". Secondly, you can't "accelerate radio waves" because radio waves are electromagnetic radiation, just like microwave photons, infrared photons, visible light photons, UV photons, X-ray photons, and Gamma-ray photons (which are all literally the same particle: photons, with just different energy), so they all travel at the same speed: the speed of light. All light travels at the same speed, always, no matter what (see: relativity), so you can't "accelerate" them. It has nothing to do with "sound waves" because the EM drive contains a vacuum chamber (in which case there is no sound because there are no molecules within it to have waves), and also it works in a vacuum (space) also of which there is no "sound".

Also, articles on the drive have not (yet) been published and confirmed by peer-reviewed journals, so until then, treat everything with skepticism.

Also also, assuming the EM drive works and does not violate the conservation of momentum (considering the fact that we have literally never found any violation of that, ever, nor evidence that it is possible), the EM drive would probably work by acting on (or "pushing against") virtual particles (a gross oversimplification). Though virtual particles have been shown to be able to exert forces on regular matter in certain situations (see: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casimir_effect ), so a propellant-less engine that pushes against virtual particles isn't that wild of a possibility.
